descriptive_title: Grade 1 Language: Demonstrations — Decoding CVC Words (B2.1-B2.3)
subject: Language

curriculum_expectations.B2.1: demonstrate phonemic awareness by manipulating individual phonemes in spoken words, including isolating, blending, segmenting, adding, deleting, and substituting phonemes
curriculum_expectations.B2.2: apply foundational knowledge of letter-sound correspondences, including consonant blends and digraphs, to read and spell unfamiliar words containing common spelling patterns
curriculum_expectations.B2.3: decode unfamiliar words containing one syllable, including words with consonant blends, digraphs, and common vowel spelling patterns

unit_overview: A 5-day Grade 1 phonics unit on decoding CVC words (B2.1-B2.3) framed around 'CVC Decoders' — Sounder Sam the Owl and Blendy the Bear. Day 1 isolates and segments phonemes (auditory only, no print). Day 2 maps letters to short-vowel sounds. Day 3 blends three sounds into CVC words. Day 4 reads CVC words in connected sentences. Day 5 closes with a Big Decoder Capstone integrating all four skills.
unit_learning_goal: Children will isolate, blend, and segment phonemes in CVC words and decode them in connected text.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Spoken words are made of separate sounds. We can ISOLATE and SEGMENT them.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can isolate and segment sounds in CVC words.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Sounder Sam claps phonemes; children segment 8 CVC words on sound boxes.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Each LETTER stands for a SOUND. CVC = consonant + vowel + consonant.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can map letters to sounds in CVC words.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Blendy maps c-a-t; children build 6 CVC words with letter cards.

lesson_arc.big_idea: BLEND sounds smoothly to read a word: /c/-/a/-/t/ slides into CAT.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can blend sounds to decode CVC words.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Sounder and Blendy blend together; children blend 10 CVC words.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Apply DECODING to read short sentences with CVC words.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can decode CVC words in a sentence.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children read 6 decodable sentences with mostly-CVC words.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Decoders HEAR sounds, MAP letters, BLEND, and READ.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can decode CVC words and read decodable text.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children rotate 4 stations: hear, map, blend, read.

recurring_characters.name: Sounder Sam the Owl
recurring_characters.role: Lead character. Phoneme guide. Anchors all 5 lessons.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A wise young owl with a sound-wave necklace and a mouth shaped like an /o/, holding a 3-cell sound box card.

recurring_characters.name: Blendy the Bear
recurring_characters.role: Decoding partner. Letter-sound and blending coach. Joins from Lesson 2.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A friendly bear holding a sound-blending strip with letter cards that slide together.

threaded_vocabulary.child_friendly_definition: A sound in a spoken word.
Break a word into separate sounds.
The sound a letter makes (not its name).
Use letter-sounds to read a word.

materials_overview: 3-Box Sound Box Cards (drawn on index cards with marker; 1 per pair)
Picture cards (cut from any source — magazines, prior worksheets, or printed; 20 per set)
Letter index cards (lowercase a-z, written in marker; 1 set per pair)
Decodable sentence strips (written in marker on card stock)
Counters (bottle caps, paper clips, dried beans — any small classroom item; 3 per pair)
OPTIONAL: a stuffed animal or sock as Sounder Sam (gestures or voice work fine)

assessment_strategy.formative: Lesson 2 letter-sound tracker; Lesson 3 blending tracker; Lesson 4 decoding tracker.

pedagogical_notes: Grade 1 SoR sequence: phonological awareness → letter-sound → blending → connected text. Maintain this order.
Day 1 stays purely AUDITORY — no print yet. Children separate sound-work from letter-work.
Use slash notation /c/-/a/-/t/ throughout teacher_script. Letter NAMES (cee, ay, tee) only when explicitly contrasting.
Picture cards must use words with predictable short-vowel CVC patterns; avoid digraphs and blends in this unit.
All required materials are everyday classroom items. Puppet is OPTIONAL — gesture and voice work fine.
canadian_context_notes: Picture set includes Canadian-friendly items (dog, sun, fox, bus, pen) — no province/region specificity needed for K-G1 phonics.
Lesson references stay neutral so teachers in any Canadian classroom can use the materials.
